evidence: Route 1 (published per-item statistics). The paper's S2 Table gives fully standardized loadings for the preliminary two-factor model on WAVE 1, the exact sample this table holds. Refitting that model on the live data (lavaan, MLR, FIML, 1710 ids) reproduces 25 of 26 to <=0.0005: scomp5 .651/.651, scomp12 .639/.639, scomp23 .594/.594, scomp26 .656/.656, scomp3 .536/.536, scomp7 .452/.452, scomp10 .526/.526, scomp15 .707/.707, scomp9 .448/.448, scomp14 .619/.619, scomp17 .614/.614, scomp22 .612/.612, scomp1 .678/.678, scomp8 .739/.739, scomp11 .593/.593, scomp16 .710/.710, scomp21 .733/.733, scomp4 .643/.643, scomp13 .656/.656, scomp18 .618/.618, scomp25 .676/.676, scomp2 .730/.730, scomp6 .681/.681, scomp20 .568/.568, scomp24 .486/.486 (published/refit). The 26th, scomp19, refits at .607 against a printed .707; S2 Table's own residual variance for that row is .631 and 1-.607^2=.632 vs 1-.707^2=.500, so the printed value is a typo for .607 -- the refit agrees with the table's arithmetic. Within each factor all 26 loadings are distinct to 3 dp, so every item is pinned to its own value and no pair can be swapped. Corroboration: the .sav marks exactly {1,8,11,16,21,4,13,18,25,2,6,20,24} '(neg)', matching Neff's reverse-scored set, and the live correlation matrix splits the same way (mean r within positives .35, within negatives .43, across .-04). NOT established by this route: which language sits in which column of a row -- the Finnish and the English come from the same S1 Table line, so that pairing is the source's, not inferred; and the resp<->option_text direction, which rests on S1 Table printing the W1 anchors in ascending 1-5 order.

No verification route needed: the IRW item codes ARE the source .sav column names. data/dwyer_2019_clinton_activism.py melts ACTIVIST_COLS=[f'Activist_{i}' for i in 1..8] with var_name='item', so no rename and no positional assignment occurs, and the .sav's own SPSS variable labels tie each of the 8 codes to its wording directly (Activist_1='Being an activist is central to who I am.'). Corroborated by the paper's two quoted sample items, Activist_1 and Activist_4 ("I make time for activism, even when I'm busy."), which match the labels character for character.
